notes.title: King of Retail 2 Demo is now Live!
notes.content:
Dear shoppers,

Do you think you have what it takes to build a retail empire from scratch? Well, prove it at King of Retail 2! We’ve just launched the demo as part of Steam NEXT Fest, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2425150/King_of_Retail_2/]available to play now[/url]!	

Start small with a modest (and pretty bare) shop, then grow it into a sprawling retail giant that customers from far and wide will come to. Stock your shelves with the items your customers actually want and decide the working fate of your employees.

[previewyoutube=2W9T12jBv-c;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]Every choice matters if you want to dominate the market.[/b]

Customize everything—your layout, décor, and product selection—to create a shopping experience that keeps customers coming back for more. Want to be the discount king, slashing prices and drawing in bargain hunters? Or maybe you’d rather run a luxury boutique catering to high-end spenders? No one’s going to question your choices—unless your profits start to dip. If they do, something may have gone wrong along the way.

And why stop at just one store? Expand across the city, conquer new neighborhoods, and adapt to every kind of customer. Every district brings fresh challenges and new opportunities, and only the sharpest business minds will thrive.

[i]But remember, just like your growing empire, this game is also a work in progress.[/i]

[b]King of Retail 2 is an ongoing project, and your feedback will help shape its future. [/b]We’re constantly refining mechanics, improving the graphics, and expanding features based on community input. This demo is just the beginning, and we’ll be reaching out to players for feedback as development continues. Your ideas and suggestions could influence the game’s next big feature or fix!

[url=https://discord.com/invite/BT4YN75cW7][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/528290da754896da4bada8e5f3787a2ff3e1938f.png[/img][/url]

If you want to stay on top of everything, follow us on our socials, especially X and [url=https://discord.com/invite/BT4YN75cW7]Discord[/url], for the latest updates, sneak peeks, and developer insights. The doors are open, the shelves are stocked. 

Download the free demo today and [b]prove you have what it takes to be crowned the King of Retail. [/b]

notes.title: Here's what's coming to King of Retail 2!
notes.content:
[b][h1][b]Hello Retailers![/b][/h1][/b]

I'm GunthorNC, Community Manager at Freaking Games, and I’ve got some thrilling news to share! As many of you know, we’re hard at work on [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2425150/King_of_Retail_2/] [b]King of Retail 2[/b][/url], a complete overhaul of the original game with a brand-new engine and a slew of exciting features. The scope of this project is [b]huge[/b], and we’re eager to give you a sneak peek of what’s in store:

[b][h2]Build Your Own Store Fixtures with Our New Display Designer![/h2][/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/21b80ab5a45ca05a4c704fa383627e1a2a23e876.png[/img]

We’re excited to introduce a game-changing feature in King of Retail 2: our [b]Custom Display Designer[/b]! This new tool empowers you to design and build your own store fixtures from the ground up, giving you unparalleled control over your store’s layout and presentation.

With the Display Designer, you can create and customize:

    [b]Shelves: [/b]Choose the size, style, and arrangement to fit your product range and store layout perfectly.
    [b]Podiums:[/b] Design display stands that highlight your best-selling or promotional items.
    [b]Freezers and Refrigerators:[/b] Customize their appearance to seamlessly integrate with your store’s aesthetic and overall design.
    [b]Spear’s:[/b] Add specialized displays for hanging candy, accessories, and other items that need to be suspended.
    [b]Clothing Racks:[/b] Design racks to showcase apparel, with options to adjust their size, style, and arrangement to fit your store's fashion needs.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/54af7d9985813f896a907991cd76cd367dc9ced0.png[/img]

Customize every aspect of your fixtures, including:

    [b]Colors:[/b] Match your store’s branding or create eye-catching contrasts.
    [b]Heights and Widths:[/b] Adjust dimensions to suit different products and store layouts.
    [b]Materials:[/b] Choose from a range of materials to achieve the perfect look and durability.
    [b]Designs:[/b] Experiment with various designs and styles to reflect your store’s unique character.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/f935a89a9c4612db213fd1193291f7adc1894561.png[/img]

Whether you want to create a sleek, modern look or a more traditional setup, our Display Designer offers endless possibilities to suit your vision. You’ll have the freedom to experiment with different configurations, ensuring that your store is both functional and visually appealing.

[b]
[h2]Design or Download Your Own Custom Maps![/h2][/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/a5edeabe5f55297e64f8a81901f6027af5c0d8f0.png[/img]

That’s right! Say goodbye to just one static map. In King of Retail 2, you can create your own customized maps or download ones made by the community. And if you prefer, you can always use the diverse map that comes with the game right out of the box.

Your store’s location will impact your customer base and business costs, adding a whole new layer of strategy to your retail empire. You’ll need to consider the various customer segments around your store location. [url=https://king-of-retail-2.fandom.com/wiki/Segments] [b]These segments represent different categories of customers[/b][/url], such as high-income professionals or blue-collar workers, each with their own preferences and expectations.

The demographics of these customer segments will influence the types of products your customers are looking for and the level of service they expect. You can choose to cater specifically to a niche customer base, tailoring your inventory and services to meet their precise needs. Alternatively, you might take a broader approach, aiming to appeal to a wider audience with a more diverse selection of products and services.

Choosing the right location and understanding its demographics will be crucial in shaping your store’s success and growing your retail empire. This feature ensures that every new map offers unique challenges and opportunities, whether you’re customizing your own or exploring the game’s built-in options.

[h2]Explore the Surroundings Outside Your Store![/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/a4a2eba64fadf7cdb4248ab94d7047787091b160.png[/img]

In King of Retail 2, your store is set in a fully realized environment. Opt for a beachfront location, and you’ll find your store right by the sea. Position your store across from a movie theater, and enjoy the bustling activity of a vibrant entertainment district. Each location is defined by its real-world context, providing a rich and immersive experience.

Instead of a static environment, you’ll interact with a setting that reflects the actual surroundings of your store. These surroundings will influence your store’s performance in various ways. For example, a location near office buildings might attract professionals who have higher expectations for goods and services, while a store near industrial areas might see more blue-collar workers who value practicality and value.

[h2][b]Real Animations Powered by Motion Tracking![/b][/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/fb11a588f23d2f97b2b17086a89b7c9b49a69d5e.gif[/img]

We’re taking realism to a whole new level with our groundbreaking motion tracking technology! In the previous game, animations were a mix of pre-made and manual. In King of Retail 2, we’ve moved beyond those limitations by using advanced motion tracking technology, the same cutting-edge equipment found in AAA games and blockbuster films.

In King of Retail 1, animations were created through traditional methods, which sometimes resulted in less fluid and less realistic body movements—or even clunky and silly-looking animations. With King of Retail 2, we’ve embraced motion capture to record every nuance of real human movement. This approach provides a significant upgrade in animation quality, delivering more lifelike and fluid character interactions that enhance your game-play experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/2c227d408affefbaeaf9198e2c1cd660f0f0e6b8.gif[/img]

You can see the difference in how characters move and interact, showcasing a new level of realism and immersion that sets King of Retail 2 apart from its predecessor.

[b][h2]Expanded Product Range – From Tiny to Huge![/h2][/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/ebde1654ecba48be2aae7eb5d9a4d13e12de0c25.gif[/img]

Not only will King of Retail 2 have more articles, They will be much better looking as well! We’ve started out with supermarket articles, but that’s just the beginning. We’re introducing new systems designed to support all kinds of products, each with its own unique storage and display requirements.

For example, frozen goods will need specialized freezers in your back room to keep them fresh, while large items like cars will require dedicated display areas that can’t be managed on standard shelves. Our system is built to accommodate everything from small everyday items to sizable appliances, ensuring that each product type is handled appropriately.

This new system adds significant depth and complexity to your store management, requiring you to carefully plan your layout and storage solutions to handle a diverse range of products effectively. Get ready to manage everything from tiny trinkets to massive appliances, each with its own distinct needs!

[h3][b]Overhauled Staff System – Coming August 31st!!![/b][/h3]

We’re deep into reimagining our staff system, and it’s going to be a game-changer. Expect staff to be a richer and more engaging experience with features like:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/a46fa9431bd6b19c84fe90b9ce533c381d654ec3.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/c681604db9fb2a0edbca0943bbf191b6702b8b7c.png[/img]

We’re excited to dive deeper into these features in the next update, so stay tuned!

Thank you for your ongoing support and enthusiasm! [b]Hundreds[/b] of players are already enjoying and testing out the game early in its current (unreleased) state, and their feedback is [b]incredibly valuable[/b] in shaping the development of the game. notes.title: Announcing King of Retail 2
notes.content:
[b][h3]Dear Retailers![/h3]

I know it has been silent from me for far too long. A lot has happened, and i deeply apologize for not keeping you in the loop about the world of King of Retail, and i can understand those of you who feel frustrated or left behind.

I have written a long post explaining why here:
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/968250/partnerevents/preview/4027975938511830174]Link to steam post[/url]
[/b]
[h3]But other than that I am proud to announce:[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/e3b8914b5dd7b421b4185c45d9941655fc7ec948.png[/img]

Production has been ongoing for some time now, and the game is in an alpha state, which it will be for a while before it is ready to enter Early Access. 

But like it was with King of Retail, i would like production to also be community driven making many of the features in the game inspired by your wishes and desires. The community have already been the source of many implementations already now.

[b]Why will King of Retail 2 be different?[/b]

The core foundation of King of Retail was built with the knowledge we had at the time when we started making the game, which was not much. Building on that foundation created many limitations down the road, making many implementations hard to do, or completely impossible without redoing major parts of the game. Furthermore the game was built using a outdated software, making many things impossible to modernize without huge, time consuming, changes as well.

So starting a new game from scratch, allows for a much more solid and futureproof foundation. That means many of the things that were missing in the original game, can now be added and improved upon. 

[list]
[*][b]Dynamic gameplay. [/b]
Jump in and out of your stores whenever you want during the day. Better simulation will make the stores feel more alive when you are not in them, increasing the dynamics and interactions between your stores. That means more things can happen, allowing higher emphasis on the CEO aspect of the game as well.

[*] [b]A whole new world. [/b]
All buildings in the city are buyable, and have a different composition of customer segments. Place your stores EXACTLY where you want. A shortened year lets you watch the seasons pass, and will require you to adapt to the requirements and the various events. Even the weather will have an influence on how your day will be.

[*][b]Multi-level stores. [/b]
You will be allowed to make stores with multiple floors. making them bigger than ever.

[*][b]More HQ options[/b]
Your HQ will be the center of all your operations, letting you manage articles, orders, staff etc. in all stores from one location. Negotiate and earn reputation with your suppliers, unlocking exclusive deals and article lines to be sold at your store. 
You will have to design your HQ, place offices and different areas, hire managers and personnel for your managers so they can perform their jobs even better.

[*][b]More differentiation. [/b]
You customers will be more unique. The Gray segment demands friendly service, but dont care about long queue times. The Blues puts less emphasis on cleanliness and service, as long as they can shop in a hurry. As your customers will be more unique, you will have to be more specific about who will be your main target group.
Articles groups will also be more unique. A grocery store, will be about managing and selling many small items, meaning bigger emphasis on storage management, but less direct sales. Electronics is more about having the right sales personnel, to convince the customers. Clothes will be heavily affected by weather and seasons, and appliances will need a separate checkout for these bulky articles.  Each category should provide a new challenge.
Articles will also change in trends, meaning your star product today, is not necessarily your star product next week requiring you to follow along on what is selling, and what is not.

[*][b]Staff changes[/b]
Staff will be more in depth, having more stats that influence their behavior. They can be organized in "teams", where their internal relationships affect their performance, learning and mood. Staff will age, and have life events happening to them. They will become more like persons, and less like robots working for you.

[*][b]More customization. [/b]
Use the new display designer to create your own unique displays. In general there will be more possibilities and more options to customize your store.

[*][b]Better graphics. [/b]
Using the new Unreal Engine, much better, and more realistic graphics will be possible. Better animations and better graphics will increase the immersion of the game.

[*]...and many, many other things.
[/list]

[b]Here are some screenshots of the current game:
[/b]
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/347b9fa817273a2e7c213b1b4eb3107c0919edeb.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/c33ebb107ad0d61a1c35103db7b4bff10edb736c.jpg[/img][/url] [url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/6e8d0719722ac629c56b4a83055f01bf0cd80437.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/b08da379f6c566bec56575c7f5ad5ce5c9ab6e56.jpg[/img][/url] [url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/6759ff45cad8e57f5d60ce321c9ea3f004397cd0.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/262e53a3b536ffe9b9d65afd5bee525410e7f913.jpg[/img][/url] [url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/2b538191b784f568cc6b0008d517ec1aa772fa6e.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/06e053f1c5ea247a75422a33342d2ec4a2730dcf.jpg[/img][/url] [url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/210685a0b2d9884c76f1b445c03355ca7995596a.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/3c96184b661581f26df3c6c7188ce29c0e4bfd1d.jpg[/img][/url]

In short King of Retail 2 will be more detailed in many of the aspects that were missing in the original game, while still sticking to the roots that made it popular to begin with, mainly being a third person retail store simulator.

If you are interested in following along, and maybe even getting access to the alpha, you can join the discord and the journey of making a new King of Retail here:

[url=https://discord.gg/BT4YN75cW7][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/528290da754896da4bada8e5f3787a2ff3e1938f.png[/img][/url]

You can also preview and wishlist King of Retail 2

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2425150/King_of_Retail_2/][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/48dc4668ba7cb6e1beb454a9027038092dcde955.png[/img][/url]

[b]That was it for now. I hope you will join in on the development of King of Retail 2, so we can make it the best game it can become.

Thanks for reading, and take care.

Kind regards
Daniel[/b]

notes.title: I am sorry for the lack of communication
notes.content:
[b]Dear Retailers![/b]

First of all, I will have to give all of you a very, very big apology for letting everything regarding King of Retail stay in the dark for so long. I know i have built up some expectations, and my intentions have always been to follow up on them, so i am truly sorry for the lack of engagement and communication over the last 1½ year. 

I can fully understand those of you who have been greatly disappointed. So now it's time for me to give you all an explanation.

Up until and after the release of King of Retail i was completely burned out. 
The process during this period was unfortunately far from optimal, and at the same time a lot of stuff happened on a personal level, leading me to an insane level of stress. 
For 4 months i slept at max 2 hours pr. night, and those were the good nights where i managed to get some actual sleep. After that, every time i tried to open Unreal (the progeam used to make the game), tried do some planning, heard a ping on Discord, etc. i within seconds felt my pulse increase drastically, and simply could not do anything, even though i felt a huge obligation to serve the community and the players. 
And i am truly, truly sorry for not responding to you for all this time.
It took me a very long time before I was able to do things relatively normal again, and when i could i needed to make a decision.

King of Retail was my first game, and my first experience of making a proper piece of software. It also had many other "firsts" along the way, and because of this the foundation of King of Retail is not as strong as i would like it to be, simply because it was built on the knowledge i had back then. This means that at the later stages, much time was spent on fixing this foundation to make it possible for new things to enter the game. And this problem will only intensify with continued work, as well as some things will be impossible to add. For instance, a simple thing like keeping multiple saves for a game is impossible without rebuilding everything.
It is also made with an old version of Unreal Engine (v. 4.22, the latest UE4 version is 4.27, and they proceeded to UE5  being on version 5.3). Many of the external plugins used have not been updated to the newer versions, meaning bringing it up to date to use the latest features, would be an immenseamount of work. 
For me it was in the end more of a frustration to work with, because every little thing i wanted to make, required me to fix some of this foundation. However it would never be what i wanted it to be, unless i redid everything from scratch. 

I have spent a lot of time thinking about what to do instead. Many ideas and many scenarios has been played through in my head. Should i continue King of Retail? Should i try a different type of game? Do i even have the desire to make games? Can i again climb this huge mountain it is to make a game as an indie developer? After a lot of thinking, i came to the conclusion that i still love my King of Retail. It has been my life for many years now. It has been my baby i brought form nothing to become a game that gave people thousands of hours of entertainment. But because of the things mentioned above, it gave more frustrantions than joy, and making a game based off of frustrations is futile when you are a solo developer, and i was also not sure how people would react if a game that was assumed dead would be brought back to revival over a year later.

I also believe that i can make something that is even better than i did before. I just need to adjust the way i did it, use the things that worked well, and discard the thigs that didn't so i don't let it go to this unhealthy level of working again. And that is why i decided to make a sequel. 

I know many of you hoped for more content to be added to the original King of Retail after final release, and i can fully understand if you are angry or frustrated. Again i can only give you my biggest apologies, but i will not keep working on King of Retail.

But by getting a fresh and proper start on a new game, i can apply all my current knowledge from the beginning, and do everything more consistently, as well as avoiding many of the bad decisions i learned along the way. This will allow a foundation that supports a much better flow of work, and will allow many of the things that I would have liked to add in the first game, and hopefully this will make for a much much better game for you to play. 

I know many will be pleased with the news, but i also know that a fair amount are disappointed or outright angry with it, which is why I dreaded making this post, and postponed it for too long. 

I am truly sorry, and it was never my intention to leave it as is 1½ years ago, and i can understand your frustrations, disappointment and anger. But i still hope you will give a warm welcome to King of Retail 2.

Thanks for reading, and take care.

Kind regards
Daniel[/b]

notes.title: GRAND OPENING: King of Retail is Fully Launched!
notes.content:
THE GRAND OPENING IS UPON US! KING OF RETAIL IS NOW FULLY LAUNCHED, OUT OF EARLY ACCESS!

Dear Retailers,
The day I've waited so long for has finally arrived. The full release of King of Retail! 

It has been a long an interesting journey, lasting more than 4 years. From starting development on an empty screen, trying to figure out [i]how do we do this???[/i] To the magic push of a button that launched the game into Early Access, where an amazing [b]five[/b] people bought the game! 😂 To the first creator video with over 1 million views on YouTube. 
I have never stopped being surprised and gratified. 

It has been a huge pleasure to interact with this community. I have been overwhelmed with your ideas and offers to help with the game in various ways. I can honestly say that this game would not be what it is today, without all of your feedback. 
Many bugs have been discovered by you, many ideas have been added directly from your suggestions, even full languages were added solely thanks to your help. I am very very thankful for all of this.

I am sorry for not having been so active lately, but planning for release, making new content, handle community management, getting COVID, and having other types of pressure from my personal life has been a lot for me to handle, and at some points I have needed a little break to clear my head and refocus again. 

However! I am so pleased that our 1.0 release is here at last! I really hope you will enjoy the changes we've made, and continue to enjoy King of Retail. To celebrate, here's a brand new gameplay trailer:

notes.title: Upcoming QoL and Feature Improvements!
notes.content:
Dear Retailers,

We are one week away from the 1.0 launch! Today, we want to talk about upcoming quality of life and feature improvements that you've been requesting. In short: some aspects of running your store were unclear (especially to new players) or needlessly tedious. The quality of life features in the launch update will greatly improve your efficiency in running your store. If you enjoy optimizing your store, this one's for you.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/278354ac36e496bc2757288e05476fa88e0b0608.png[/img]

Managing your articles could be a bit of a hassle sometimes, especially in bigger stores with lots of different sales going on at once. We've spent quite a bit of time improving on the existing systems in King of Retail. Let's start with ordering articles.

[h3]IDs, Tags, and Notes[/h3]
A good retail manager is always on top of what comes in, what goes out, and at what price. To make specific articles more searchable, every article now has a unique ID that you can use to search for it. Those of you who have worked in retail will probably be familiar with the concept.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/3f55bae109269ab8457a6d0d274f5fc86b021dc9.png[/img]

IDs are for when you [i]really[/i] want a specific article, but a more customizable option is the new [i]tag[/i] system.

You can add a custom tag to any item by simply typing it in. Afterwards, you can type in your tag in the search bar, and find all the tagged products. This is a great way to group articles by color, aesthetic, or any other metric you can think of.

Also, tags are saved [i]per manager[/i], so you won't have to re-type them if you start a new store!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/e6347d4b8fa08894e436f0395aaf9468ae2c629d.gif[/img]

Lastly, you can add notes to articles. Maybe an article sold particularly well during a certain event in town? That's worth adding a note for, in case the event happens again! Or maybe you want to remind yourself when the item was last on sale to plan your strategy?

[h3]Article Screen[/h3]
You may have already spotted some improvements in the screenshots above to the article screen itself. With this new screen, you will have all the information you need at your disposal, like how well the article is selling amongst different demographics, allowing you to further optimize your store.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/a917441ef94888533f68103f9229f093bd301869.png[/img]

Another improvement is that you will be able to see these details anywhere! No longer do you need to visit the office to see specific metrics, but you can pull those stats up during a workday as well. This also means you can more easily plan sales on the fly. Simply press Q when selecting an article, and you can see its details and edit its price.

Speaking of editing its price, this change also allows you to easily put specific articles on sale, rather than having to create discounts per display. That means you can now quickly adjust prices on the fly, adapting to your customer's need more efficiently.

[h3]Mirroring[/h3]
A small but often-requested QoL feature is that you'll be able to mirror inventory! In the case of registers, that means you can control whether people will enter the queue from the left or right side. A lot of you were quite particular about this, so here it is!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/7488043b3f3b92521ee478ea96338cf7178416ef.gif[/img]

[h3]Loans at the Bank[/h3]
And for the campaign players, one commonly requested feature was to take out loans (curiously, no one ever requested being able to [i]pay those loans back[/i]). The new bank area will allow you to do just that, provided you have some capital.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/4a9aa98b2147800ebdb130fe9d2291b80737617c.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/90d0fdb053540324bf13b511565a07d54addc017.png[/img]

[h3]Graphics Optimization[/h3]
The last QoL change we wanted to mention in this blog is that we've put a lot of time into optimizing King of Retail's textures and meshes. This can result in up to 30% more FPS than in previous versions!

There's more improvements in 1.0, like security perks for staff and [i]lots[/i] of bug fixes, but we'll save those for next week — see you then!

notes.title: V. 0.17 Released - Do you plan to pay for those?
notes.content:
Dear Retailers

So after a christmas, new years and a bit of time off, we are now back with a new update for you. Let's have a look of what it contains.

[b]--- Thieves ---[/b]

First of all, a new feature that many of you have requested for quite along time has been added. Thieves will enter your stores and take your stuff.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/74f59d7248c43bcd98d347af120d5fd3ffe48bfd.png[/img]

Thieves will look very suspicious when taking articles. So if you see a thief hurry to them and kick them out of your store. You can also assign the new "Security" role to your staff, and they will also try and catch thieves.

You can also buy various security alarms to help you catching the thieves.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/42b77c48fedeaa352ad8f43c457354554082b921.png[/img]

[b]--- Competitors ---[/b]

In campaign mode, competitors will now also arrive to the city, and try to earn money by taking customers away from you. They will open up stores in various areas, and if you are selling the same articles, the battle is on.

Can you survive their impact and run them out of business, or will you be the one suffering too many losses?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/4eccaacb57682557cecca13f00cd4ccef5645a55.jpg[/img]

These competitors can do marketing campaigns to try and push you even further. But fortunately you can also now do marketing. You can bring attention to your own stores, or directly attack the competitors to push them even further, and try and run their stores out of business.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/90733fa4d1c50d4ac928d3d868bf0a3afd829e98.png[/img]

[b]--- General improvements of campaign mode ---[/b]

- Added tutorials to the HQ

The HQ is a very confusing place for new players, and not much help was given in finding your way around it. Now info markers are placed everywhere, so you have a better idea of what possibilities you have in the various areas.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/9d6f1c587624f7a58f19a03f89f9a4b342e0157f.png[/img]

- Various guides

Also many of the actions were kind of hard to set up correctly for a new player, and involved many actions in various areas that allowed for various mistakes.

Some of these has now been changed, such that creating a concept, as well as aquiring a new store has been made simpler.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/a5c3383638102fb27dc6607bf1f5a764d623b3fc.png[/img]

- More careers

You can also now start a career in a different direction. So instead of joining Armina, you now also go with Electronic Bee and sell electronics instead,

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/196fa836d1f982bb7f19c985bd25e43cde0d7909.png[/img]

- Other minor improvements

Many other minor improvements has been added to the campaign mode, so it's easier and more intuitive to find your way around. 

That is all for this update. I hope you will enjoy the update and the new changes to the game.
Reports of bugs and general feedback are most welcome, so don't hesitate to post. You are also very welcome to join the community at our discord channel.

[url=https://www.Discord.gg/fckN6bE][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/2d23cbd46a7bf387d488e366c7d3f547ff26728d.png[/img][/url]

Until next time, have a happy sale.
//Daniel

notes.title: Version 0.16.0 released - How do I look?
notes.content:
[b]Dear Retailers!

It is time for yet another update to King of Retail. 

During this past year I have been blessed with having the assistance of my graphics artist who has added and upgraded a lot of things in the game, which have given a great lift to the overall visuals, as well as allowing me to focus more on programming and implementing new features. 
But as the game gets bigger and bigger, much time goes into managing things that doesn't directly impact the game features themselves. Playtesting, balancing, bug hunting, translation management and so on. 

And now I am very pleased to say that another person has joined the team, making it a grand total of 3 people working directly on King of Retail. 
She will be assisting me in doing many of these tasks, as well as adding new stuff to the game as she also is quite capable with Photoshop. 
So I am looking much forward to this, and I hope we will be able to make King of Retail even more enjoyable for you to play.

But on to the actual changes. 
For a long time we have been preparing and designing new characters to bring a much more diverse looking population to the game, instead of having all residents in the city looking all the same.
Let us have a look of what have been added.[/b]



[h2]--- New faces ---[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/74798daffb5290a507c44eca54ccacf532c04476.png[/img]

Instead of having 2 faces to choose from, we changed it into a slider system, where you can adjust the facial traits with more detail. You can also freely select hair color, as well as select between more, better looking hair styles.



[h2]--- New Outfits ---[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/64872ead5442e212f6c6c4f709fc2a301c1426f7.png[/img]

Before this update, all customers in your store wore the same clothes. But that is over now, as they have received unique clothings that better fit their individual segment.



[h2]--- Staff Uniforms ---[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/07f7ceab821200e42aeff4ff0b3e80ea8848ccfb.png[/img]

It is also now possible to design your own uniforms for your various stores and concepts. Should your staff have a simple, or an exclusive look. Tailor the outfit to match the look of the rest of your store.



[h2]--- Bugs & Small conveniences ---[/h2]

[h2]- Minimum storage system[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/f9966905dc42da5cc08acde081632089627f7cf0.png[/img]

Many of you have also requested an easier use of the minimum storage system, so now it's possible to add directly to this when ordering an article, making it much easier to setup when starting a new store.

[h2]- Keybindings[/h2]

Keybinds did not save between closing and opening the game, this should be fixed so you don't have to remap the keys every time.

[h2]- Color picker[/h2]

It was time to look at an old and popular request which is a bit over due. But now the color picker has been updated such that you have complete control in selecting the exact color that you want. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/f9bd1315c4577c2144972768ecc7021ef5cc5df3.png[/img]


[h2]--- Up next ---[/h2]

[h3]- New environments[/h3]
My graphics artist has been done for a while with these new characters as the last work is always implementing the actual things to the game. So she is already making good progress with the next big graphical update, which is new environments.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/90f171a64b18ef02ffcf95260bfe83e32fc3342a.png[/img]

So soon you will finally have variety in the areas where you manage your stores, and they will better exemplify the area you are in, in the campaign mode. Plus, they look much nicer than the existing area that i could conjure up back in the day.

[h3]- Thieves[/h3]
With the new characters and skills, it's about putting it a bit to use. A very popular request during all of the development period has been thieves in the stores. So i thought i would finally accomodate this request, and allow you to take on the battle with these persons that doesn't want to pay for your hard earned in game articles.

[h3]- New careers[/h3]
When campaign mode was introduced, clothes was the only existing type of article in the game, which is why there only exist these career paths where you sell clothes. So to add to the diversity a bit, we will be working on adding more of these, so this starting phase can vary a bit from time to time.



[b]That was it for this update.
As always, I am very interested in listening to new ideas, bug reports and what else you might have to tell.

You are also more than welcome to join our Discord!

Until next time, have a great sale
//Daniel[/b]

notes.title: V. 0.15.0 released - We should have a talk
notes.content:
[b]Dear Retailers!

It has been quite some time since the last update, and I apologize for that. A lot has been changed, i have taken a vacation, and had eye surgery that I needed to recover from. So that is the reason behind the lack of updates in the last period. But now the update is ready, and there has also been made actual work that is ready for the next one, so we have not been sitting idle by.

But let's move on to the actual changes of this update.[/b]

[h2]--- Staff Overhaul ---[/h2]
The focus of this update has been on improving many areas of how your staff works. Many of the changes has largely been based on requests from all of you in the community.

[h3]- The role designer[/h3]
Many of you have been annoyed with your staffs efficiency, where they would stand around if there was nothing more to do.
This has been changed with a complete overhaul of their job system.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/e65dfd8779e68b7586ffdc7c94670d3e8af58b70.png[/img]

Now instead of them having one task to do, you can now customize their roles, and create as many as you want. This means that you can have one employee go and unpack articles, and after that task is done, to start selling to the customers in the store. 
Another employee can selling as the primary task, and refill the displays in the meantime. 
So the control of which tasks, and how they should prioritize them is entirely up to you.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/c2b176c67c5c5be4f2c8d7f772d9837987332c43.png[/img]

On top of this, you can assign these on an hourly basis. So an employee can be a restocker from 9-12, and be a cashier from 12-17 if that is what you want.

So full control of your staffs tasks in every hour of the day. And for those of you that don't want to go into this level of micromanagement, this system also has the same ease of use as the old one, as you can quicly assign a simple task for the entire day as well.

[h3]- The greeter[/h3]
Thanks to the new system, it is now much easier for me to add new tasks to the game. So one of these additions is the new greeter task.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/acb3ef66449cb3d46aec110ee94de59de1a29b1f.png[/img]

This finally allows for something many of you have dreamed of for a long, long time. More precisely for you to be able to send your employees outside the store to try and convince the customers to go into the store. So no more standing outside and doing endless conversations to get one more customer into the store.

[h3]- New skill system[/h3]
The old talent system ensured that all staff eventually would be equally good at everything. This gave the feeling of the staff not really having any difference from each other.
Instead this has been replaced by a new skill/perk system.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/8ca3fe6b161bf62bb7d37f55c464a36c364589ce.png[/img]

First of all, in this system all staff can do all tasks to begin with. So no more sending them on courses to make them able to stand at the cash register.
Instead they have various skill points regarding the various tasks, and learn each skill at various speeds. Yes in time this also means that all staff can become equally good in the end, but it is highly individual when they will reach this point.

And to ensure their individuality, various perks have been introduced. This means that each employee can have a set amount of favorite customer types, favorite article categories and specialized perks that makes this person more unique at a certain area.

So now it can generate higher profits, if you think more about the scheduling and placement of your employees during the day.

[h3]- Staff motivation[/h3]
During the day it has never really been possible to influence your staff directly during the day. 
Yes, you had the possibility to send them on a break, but nothing more than that.
This has also changed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/3219d29cb5ca3efd410bb7a815c090c7decd415a.png[/img]

Now you can go directly to each employee and conduct personal talks with them. Here you can give them an optimistic morale boost, as well as a stern reminder for them to pick up the pace.

This will influence their mood and their new productivity stat they have received. 
Productivity, combined with familiarity, energy and skill determines how fast they will perform a given task. 
This will give you a top performance from a happy, productive, well rested worker that has been around for quite some time. 
So spending time managing your staff in depth can give you an edge which will generate higher profits. Although if this is not your thing, your store should still be able to run rather smooth still.

On top of this you can also see the things that currently affect the mood an productivity of your staff, such that you can react on this.

[h3]- New courses[/h3]
With these changes the old courses was obsolete, and frankly, you needed to send your staff on too many courses in general.
So this system changed as well.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/d27b2bc0803de66b459042e5fd2d4ae12fffb25a.png[/img]

When your employee has reached a certain level, you can send the person on a course to gain a new set of perks, chosen by you. 

A different type of course, the Booster Course, has also been added.
When an employee has been sent on a booster course, their learning is improved by a lot the following week.

[h2]--- Woman's Bottoms ---[/h2]

For the last update a lot of work has gone into adding a women's clothing category. However it was not finished. Now the addition of a new set of items has been added.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/1829d63ae81063eeb2e64f48e53f9db58ce59581.png[/img]

This completes this category so far.

[h2]--- Bugs and ideas ---[/h2]

As usual, bugs might be hiding around somewhere after a major update like this, and i will be ready to fix major issues quickly, so don't hesitate to report anything you might find, both here and on our Discord.
Also feedback and ideas are as always very welcome.

[h2]--- Up next ---[/h2]

As mentioned we have already prepared at bit for the next update. 
My graphics artist has been spending a lot of time on upgrading the characters in the game, so the future will bring much better and different characters, customizable uniforms, morphing system for heads, allowing you to customize the face of characters, improved hairstyles and more.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/e7370a21fb102da7cb011ad13969823a0568ad9e.png[/img]

notes.title: V. 0.14 available - Ready For Women's Clothing
notes.content:
[b]Dear Retailers!

After a lot of work, we can finally release the next big update, giving you even more stuff to do in the game. Without further ado, let's dive into what's new in this update![/b]


[h2]--- Women's clothing ---[/h2]

So first of all, the biggest change is the introduction of a completely new category. Women's clothing.
For now this contains the two sub categories Tops and Shoes, which feature around 200 articles each, so plenty of new things to put into your stores.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/2672172d89771be124b062a9bb152b42b76c8731.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/54d1ee656a907f306886b0d3ad8aed36533d9123.png[/img]

These also contain some new types, such as dresses and boots, which can't fit on the regular clothing displays, which means a bunch of new displays have been made. However these work the other way around, so normal shoes also fit on these boots displays, meaning that your existing clothing stores also can use these new displays.

[h3]- New displays[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/d3ddde02d1d996a259c52fa4168bb5eb35e2cb81.png[/img]

The different types of clothing and shoes vary a bit in price range and luxury, meaning that there should be both fast and slow selling articles, which then require various amount of effort to sell.


[h2]--- Staff upgrades ---[/h2]

We've also introduced some new tools for managing your staff.

[h3]- Staff zoning[/h3]
First of all a new zoning system for your staff has been added. With this you can control each person at work, and tell them where they should be working. 
Maybe you want a team of salespersons close to the computers, and a team of stocking experts near the groceries? This is perfectly possible now. Decide whether your staff should roam free or stay fixed, depending on what makes most sense at your current store.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/20842fdcb57ee2c10fed4163a0e79db305b859f6.png[/img]

[h3]- Staff notes[/h3]
It is also possible to write notes to yourself about your staff. Explain how you schedule, or other important stuff for you to remember next time you look at that the person.


[h2]--- General options ---[/h2]

It was also about time to introduce some other general options to the game, as you have requested.

First of all, it is now possible to bind some of the keys in the game. Many of you playing with AZERTY layouts have been complaining that the keys are unintuitive. So now you can set them to your liking.

And an FOV slider has also been added for people playing in wider monitors, as well as a few various mouse settings have been added.

I am very open for ideas to even more options you would like to see implemented.


[h2]--- Change of game fundamentals ---[/h2]

The above are the updates that have made it into the game. And it might not seem as a lot given the time used for this update. 
However a lot of work has been made to change the base structure of the game. Many of these structures were made when we first started building the game, which also was a time where we didn't know much about building, preparing and managing a project of this size. 
This means these foundations were not optimal, but instead of dedicating time to change it, new features were built on top instead. But this became more and more of a problem, and some things that are planned in the future would simply not be possible with this, so now it needed to change.

To be specific, is was how all data for articles and staff was setup and handled. So this means that everywhere in the game where the manager, an article or staff was used needed to be changed. And as you can guess this is almost everywhere in the game, so it meant quite a lot to change.

But now it's finally done, and it should mean it will be easier to add new features to the game.


[h2]--- Whats next ---[/h2]

So what will we start working on. Well, my amazing graphics artist has already begun production of bottoms for the women's wear, so that will most likely be ready for the next large update of the game.

I will be adding more flexibility to managing your staff. 
One of these is to allow you to custom tailor their work, so they can prioritize multiple tasks. 

- Should a person fill displays, and then go to the cash register if there is not more to fill?
- Should a person unpack deliveries, and then go outside and pull customers in?

This should allow your staff to be more versatile, as well as minimizing down time where they do nothing.


[h2]--- Bugs ---[/h2]

This version has been through a quite lengthy beta period, so hopefully most of the bugs from all of this have been found, but we all know there's bound to be a couple sneaking around out there. So please keep on reporting these, as it is very helpful for me to track them down and remove them. 
I will be on standby for the next days to remove major ones that might be uncovered.

[b]That was it for this update.

Our Discord is becoming very big with lots of active people on there, and it is very nice to see how helpful you are to each other. It is very appreciated.

You can join it at: 

[url=https://www.Discord.gg/fckN6bE][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/2d23cbd46a7bf387d488e366c7d3f547ff26728d.png[/img][/url]

I will head back and create some more content for you to use.
Happy sales

//Daniel[/b]

notes.title: Version 0.13.1 released - How does it work again?
notes.content:
[b]Dear Retailers!

It is time for yet another update to King of Retail. The primary focus has been on easing the onboarding for new players, and to better explain many of the game's mechanics to those that want to go deep into the micromanagement aspect of the game. So lets get to it.[/b]

[h2]--- Tutorials ---[/h2]
Many of you have reported difficulties when starting the game and learning some of the terms and mechanics that exist in the game. Also the existing ones were in much need of an upgrade, as they were outdated.
So much has been changed, and replaced with a new system that makes it easier for me to maintain and add new stuff when the need for it arises. 

[h3]- Business School[/h3]
At the main menu as well as at the university in campaign mode you can access the business school. Here you find the more explanatory tutorials presented as small courses you can take on various subjects.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/c2cfba4bc8d884a458e6def85222da87dc521819.png[/img]

[h3]- Campaign[/h3]
Getting into the campaign mode has been a bit confusing for many to find their way around it all, given that the only vague explanations are at the City Hall. These are still there, but now you also have a more bullet point type of tutorial that will assist you along the road, which hopefully will make this experience a lot easier and more understandable.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/d2767ef3948aa03b5b23f3406524e484678bae44.png[/img]

[h3]- In store[/h3]
The in store tutorial looks almost the same, but it has more tasks now that will bring you more around the store, giving you a better chance to understand what is possible at the store. 

[h3]- Office[/h3]
The office tutorial was the last remaining part with looks from the old UI. This has been changed to look like the rest of the game. 

[h2]--- New Articles ---[/h2]
Focus in this patch has not been so much on adding content, but we have still managed to add a new pack of shoes to the game. 
This was a bit underrepresented compared to the rest of the categories in clothing, which is why we decided to complete this category.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/35a6fe36f1a2b3c3f0da3eecd0c12e666d826077.png[/img]

[h2]--- Logos ---[/h2]
To the ones that haven't experimented with their own logos, there is now a much bigger selection to choose from when designing your stores, compared to the previous four to select from. Hopefully it will bring some variation to your stores and corporations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/3b6e7b734cecc65bed5d7cfc514d8108bde62076.png[/img]

[h2]--- Quality of Life ---[/h2]
As you can see there has not been work on one massive feature alone, but development has been diversified a bit. A part of this was adding many minor changes to existing features and screens,

[h3]- Article overlay[/h3]
This has been updated so you have much more information available when looking at the article. As many has requested it also shows if the article is present at the store, making it easier to find any articles that are only taking up space in storage.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/7154d87826fb94cd3413f46d325ba0a7321df47a.png[/img]

[h3]- Set task for all days[/h3]
You can now set an employee to do one task all week with one button, instead of having to do it individually for each day.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/bd75925ec19c668fc525429c01b55f3628284bea.png[/img]

[h3]- Options at office[/h3]
When you press "Escape" at the office, you now have access to the regular menu. Here you can also revisit the office tutorial if that is your desire.

[h3]- Minor UI changes[/h3]
Other than the above many screens have in general received small tweaks here and there. Nothing big and noticeable, but small details that should improve the overall usage. 
During the next period work on improving existing screens will still continue.

[h3]- Bugs[/h3]
Also some minor bugs have been fixed, and I am very appreciative of bugs you find and report. Even though they are not fixed immediately they all go to my list of things I need to look at, so please continue to report stuff you might find in game.

[h2]--- New Art---[/h2]
With all of these in-game changes, I couldn't leave the game's art behind. We've worked hard with an artist to create this brand new cover art for King of Retail!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/6da99490e97c846004ed1eaf565011d4c4d1e8c7.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/9ede1ebf561ba219fab17136430acf739bbe78ee.jpg[/img]

[h2]--- Whats next? ---[/h2]
Those were the major changes for this version. And we are already preparing for the next one. It is not fully planned how much it will contain, but I can at least tell some of the things we intend to do.

The reason we haven't got that many new articles in this update is because we also have been working on a new category. My super fantastic graphics artist has been spending many hours on making various women's shoes and clothes. 
There is still work to do on this, as the plan is that it can be playable with a large selection of articles from the next update.

notes.title: Store Design Contest WINNERS!
notes.content:
Dear retailers,

We're excited to announce the four winners of our store design contest. This was a very difficult contest to judge -- we honestly didn't expect all of the entries to be [i]this[/i] good. After careful consideration and lots of trying to convince each other of our favorite picks, we finally have a list of winners.

[h2]Category winners[/h2]
Below are our favorite stores in the [i]Clothing, Electornics, and Supermarket[/i] categories.

[h3]Clothing - Kathy's[/h3]
Our first winning store is [b]Kathy's[/b] by Discord user Kathy. We see a lot of stores filled to the brim with articles and posters, but this one favors a clean and simple design. It's reminiscent of those fancy clothing stores that offer quality over quantity in their catalog, making for large, minimalist, and open floor plans. 

We also particularly love the staff room, with its trendy wall design.

(And yes, we are aware that the image has been touched up in post, but that had no influence over the vote!) 

[url=https://i.imgur.com/Tg3XkWE.jpg][img]https://i.imgur.com/Tg3XkWE.jpg[/img][/url]
[url=https://i.imgur.com/OsK66ff.jpg][img]https://i.imgur.com/OsK66ff.jpg[/img][/url]
[url=https://i.imgur.com/mehL8T0.jpg][img]https://i.imgur.com/mehL8T0.jpg[/img][/url]


[h3]Electronics - C'tech[/h3]
Our winner in the Electronics category is [b]C'tech[/b] by Discord user El Caponey. Right away, we loved the attention to detail in creating a 'returns' section. Even though there are no returns in the game, it made the store feel even more alive and realistic.

Second, the little 'alcoves' filled with different articles was a unique approach that we don't see every day. While the color scheme was a [i]bit[/i] much on the eyes, the floor plan and article placement cemented this store as our favorite in the Electronics department.

[previewyoutube=qDQt-XD8zZI;full][/previewyoutube]


[h3]Supermarket - Designer Drunk[/h3]
And the final category winner is [b]Designer Drunk[/b] by Discord user Lemongrass. While the name might imply that some alcoholic beverages were consumed in the making of this store, we didn't notice. The store wears its theme on its sleeve: retro and disco. 

From the lava lamp logo on the doors, to the somewhat trippy patterns on the floors and walls, Designer Drunk maintains a very consistent style. You can imagine inebriated customers coming in after a night of clubbing to pick up some more booze (or hamburgers?).

[url=https://i.imgur.com/WM1CJ20.jpg][img]https://i.imgur.com/WM1CJ20.jpg[/img][/url]


[h3]Grand Prize winner - All-in[/h3]
Drum roll please...

The grand prize winner, our #1 pick, is [b]All-in[/b] by Discord user Gastong. Simply put, this store has everything. A consistent color scheme, lots of labeled article sections, tons of custom posters, and the "Please wear a mask" signs were a nice touch. Out of all the entries, this store was most likely to actually exist out there in the wild (well, apart from the poster behind the counter).

[previewyoutube=IuUWEBHad7M;full][/previewyoutube]

Thank you to everyone who participated! Again, this was a seriously difficult competition to judge, and every entry had a shot at winning. And to the winners, we'll be in touch soon regarding prizes!

notes.title: King of Retail: Store Design Contest!
notes.content:
Dear Retailers,

As some of you may have noticed, our community has grown quite a bit recently. We’ve been seeing a lot of entertaining Twitch streamers pick up the game and introduce their viewers to our little neck of the Steam store. That’s why we’re organizing a fun contest for you all to participate in!


[h2]Store design contest[/h2]
The title says it all! Being good with numbers is one thing, but a great retail manager also has a keen eye for designing a store. Setting the right price doesn’t matter if your store doesn’t look good in the first place. A great store provides an atmosphere that almost makes it impossible for the customer not to enter the store and suddenly feel they need everything you sell.

[h2]Rules[/h2]
[list]
[*] Three categories you can enter in: electronics, clothing, and supermarkets. You can enter one store per category.
[*] Store must be at least 15 blocks large.
[*] Must submit either screenshots or a video in the #store-design-contest channel [url=https://discord.gg/YquDPGkTsM]on Discord[/url] (videos are preferred!)
[*] You are allowed (and honestly, encouraged) to use the beta branch cheat menu. This way, everyone can be on equal footing.
[*] You are allowed to make your own custom logos and posters.
[*] You have until [u][b]Friday April 23rd[/b][/u] to submit your store(s)!
[/list]

[u][b]To switch to the beta branch:[/b][/u]
[olist]
[*]Right-click King of Retail in your Steam library
[*]Click 'Properties'
[*]Click 'Betas'
[*]In the drop-down menu, select 'beta'
[*]Your game should now update to the beta branch. In game, press [b]Z[/b] to bring up the cheat menu!
[/olist]

[i]Note: your usual managers and stores won't be available on the beta branch. Your saves aren't gone, they're just on the regular branch, so don't panic![/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/d5213426360281a395489e39515210a70cf57910.gif[/img]


[h2]What will I be judged on?[/h2]

You will be judged on two main things:

[b]Design[/b], meaning the overall look of the store. Consider things like:
[list]
[*] Do your colors and materials complement each other well?
[*] Are your displays consistently designed?
[*] Are your signs attention-grabbing without being annoying?
[/list]
[b]Floorplan[/b], meaning [i]does your store make sense?[/i]
[list]
[*] Is it sorted into minor departments that would make it easy for a customer to use?
[*] Does the layout make for a sensible way for the customers to move around?
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/553d1282dcd9ba6f674a69fd549a2f3780607c32.jpg[/img]

[h2]Prizes[/h2]

There will be four winners in total -- one for each category, and one best [i]overall[/i] store. No matter how incredible your stores look, you can only win [b]one[/b] prize. The managers of the best store in each of the three categories will:

[list]
[*] Receive three King of Retail Steam keys to give away to friends.
[*] Get to write a spam e-mail that will randomly appear in-game for other players! Are you a foreign prince looking for a loan, are you part of a pyramid scheme, or a cult? Express your creativity!
[/list]

The manager of the [b]best overall store[/b] will:
[list]
[*] Receive five King of Retail Steam keys to give away to friends.
[*] Get a piece of clothing with their own name/design in the game!
[/list]
[i]Note: we reserve the right to edit your e-mails or designs. No bigotry, misogyny, etc. -- keep things PG 13.[/i]

[h2]Tips![/h2]
[list]
[*] Use the beta branch (instructions above!) cheat menu so you won't have to worry about money!
[*] Want to create beautiful posters, but don't own Photoshop? Use free alternatives like [url=https://www.gimp.org/]Gimp[/url] or [url=https://www.photopea.com/]Photopea.[/url]
[*] Check out the tutorial below to truly master the poster maker!
[/list]

[previewyoutube=4ayMB6DevbY;full][/previewyoutube]

And that's it! We hope you're as excited as we are to see everyone's creations. Don't forget to have fun with it, and don't stress yourself out too much -- there's bound to be more contests in the future.

Happy sales.

I am also beginning the steps of adding some more flesh to the campaign experience itself. Initially this is done by adding various parcel companies to the game. In the current build, all of your articles are delivered when your store opens. This will become more of a luxury after this patch, as each delivery company will have its pros and cons.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/67b17a1c266b7b9be01ad1662ecae0bd5c68f876.png[/img]

They can now be late, forget some of your articles, deliver at specific hours, carry different amounts and some might not allow extra deliveries. The better companies are more expensive to make a deal with, so find a solution that isn't too costly for your current business.
You can find this inside your HQ.

Those of you already playing campaign mode might want to negotiate thias as soon as possible, as it now contains limitations on the amount of articles that is delivered.


[h2]--- Negotiating system ---[/h2]

To do this I decided for an improved negotiation system. This will also feature in some of the future implementations as well. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34023693/be6e2fbab5feccdab612610d21f8e3a7483e2848.png[/img]


[h2]--- Minor Changes ---[/h2]

[h3]- Article advertisements[/h3]
Basically already added to the game, as it got uploaded in a hotfix. But it's now possible at your office to advertise specific articles in the magazine, creating a hype to try and boost the sales for that particular one.

[h3]- Talent speeds[/h3]
Some mentioned that it was too easy to get highly talented staff in high population areas. So now this has been taken into account, making it require more actions from your staff to increase in level when populations are higher.

[h3]- Adding day when leaving game[/h3]
There has also been a persisting bug that added an extra day if you left the game while in the store. This should also not be happening any more.

[h3]- Proper use of exits[/h3]
The AI's should be better at using the proper entrance and exits now.

[h2]--- Community ---[/h2]
The discord is becoming a more and more active place to be, with many contributing of various kind. It's very humbling to see all of this energy you are using to create various stuff.
